title: Stop building a schema checker for every upload

blocks.text: Partners upload order documents, and the upload service checks each one against the partner schema before accepting it. A `Checker` compiles the schema when it is built, which costs a lot of CPU and memory, and it keeps state between calls, so one thread at a time may use it. The service used to run uploads on a pool of 16 platform threads and kept one checker per pool thread. It now runs every upload on a virtual thread of its own, and at the last partner deadline the instances spent more CPU building checkers than checking documents.
Operations has settled on a limit: the service may hold at most `max` checkers. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/SchemaChecks.java`:

items: `borrow()`: hands out a checker for one upload;
`check(document)`: checks one document on the calling upload's thread.

blocks.text: When you're done, any number of uploads in flight build at most `max` checkers, an upload that finds them all busy waits for one, no checker is ever used by two uploads at once, and a document that makes its checker throw doesn't leave the service short of a checker. About twelve lines in total, including the fields you add.
The tests send each upload on a virtual thread of its own, count the checkers built, and hold checks in progress to see who uses which checker.

cases.says: twenty-five uploads checked at the same time each get the right verdict
twelve uploads, each on its own virtual thread, build no more checkers than the limit of three
with a limit of one checker, an upload whose document can't be read fails, and the next upload is still checked
while three uploads are being checked at once, no checker is in use by two of them

origin.section: One Thread per Task Means Nothing Per-Thread Is Reused: Pool the Expensive Object, Not the Thread

concepts: The expensive, non-thread-safe object is pooled with a bound, borrowed per task and given back on every path, while each task keeps its own virtual thread.
